title: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act

claims.claim: The IRS Whistleblower Program pays awards to whistleblowers, tied to the proceeds the IRS collects in the matters they report.
claims.sourceSpan: all of the proceeds resulting from actions subject to the award recommendation have been collected
claims.note: Plain-English framing of the award program from the bill's own references to whistleblower awards and collected proceeds.

claims.claim: The Tax Court must review IRS award determinations de novo, based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination plus any newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence.
claims.sourceSpan: Any review by the Tax Court under the preceding sentence shall be de novo and shall be based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination and any additional newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence

claims.claim: Whistleblowers may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court unless the court finds a societal interest in disclosure that exceeds the potential harm to the whistleblower.
claims.sourceSpan: a whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court for all proceedings under this section absent a finding by the Tax Court that a societal interest exists
claims.note: Reconciled to Engrossed: text reads 'may elect' (optional). The superseded Introduced text read 'shall proceed anonymously' (mandatory).

claims.claim: Awards accrue interest when the IRS does not provide a preliminary award recommendation notice before a set date.
claims.sourceSpan: If the Secretary has not provided notice to an individual described in paragraph (1) of a preliminary award recommendation before the applicable date, the amount of any award under this subsection shall include interest from such date at the overpayment rate under section 6621(a)
claims.note: 'IRS' = 'the Secretary' (Secretary of the Treasury or delegate) per Section 1(c).

claims.claim: The IRS whistleblower report must include a list of up to 10 top tax avoidance schemes disclosed by whistleblowers.
claims.sourceSpan: a list and descriptions of the top tax avoidance schemes, not to exceed 10, disclosed by whistleblowers during such year

claims.claim: The attorney's-fee deduction is broadened from section 7623(b) awards to all section 7623 awards.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 62(a)(21)(A)(i) is amended by striking ``7623(b)'' and inserting ``7623''
claims.note: Cross-reference change 7623(b) -> 7623 broadens the deduction to the whole whistleblower award section. The removed 'discretionary vs mandatory' labels (in the pre-reconciliation prose) named subsection contents not stated in the bill text.

claims.claim: The bill makes five changes to the program (Sections 2 through 6).
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 2. Standard and scope of review of whistleblower award determinations. Sec. 3. Whistleblower privacy protections. Sec. 4. Modification of IRS whistleblower report. Sec. 5. Interest on whistleblower awards. Sec. 6. Correction regarding deductions for attorney's fees.
claims.note: Count = five substantive sections (2-6); Section 1 is short title/definitions.

claims.claim: Makes five changes to the IRS whistleblower award program: de novo Tax Court review, an anonymity election, interest on delayed preliminary award recommendation notice, an expanded whistleblower report, and a broader attorney's-fee deduction.
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 2. Standard and scope of review of whistleblower award determinations. Sec. 3. Whistleblower privacy protections. Sec. 4. Modification of IRS whistleblower report. Sec. 5. Interest on whistleblower awards. Sec. 6. Correction regarding deductions for attorney's fees.
claims.note: Compound restatement of the five substantive sections; each element backed by its own section row below.

claims.claim: Tax Court must now review IRS whistleblower award decisions de novo (from scratch).
claims.sourceSpan: Any review by the Tax Court under the preceding sentence shall be de novo
claims.note: Removed the pre-reconciliation clause 'not just for unreasonableness' — the prior standard is not stated in the bill text and no referencedSource is registered.

claims.claim: Applies to petitions pending on or filed after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: apply to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 which are pending on, or filed on or after, the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Whistleblowers may elect anonymity in Tax Court, subject to a societal-interest exception.
claims.sourceSpan: a whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court for all proceedings under this section absent a finding by the Tax Court that a societal interest exists
claims.note: Reconciled: 'public interest' in pre-reconciliation prose replaced with source term 'societal interest'; 'may elect' reflects Engrossed optional phrasing.

claims.claim: Interest accrues on awards when IRS misses its preliminary recommendation deadline.
claims.sourceSpan: the amount of any award under this subsection shall include interest from such date at the overpayment rate under section 6621(a)
claims.note: 'deadline' = the 'applicable date' before which the notice must be given.

claims.claim: Attorney fee deduction broadened from one whistleblower award category to all of them.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 62(a)(21)(A)(i) is amended by striking ``7623(b)'' and inserting ``7623''

claims.claim: IRS report must list up to 10 top tax avoidance schemes disclosed by whistleblowers.
claims.sourceSpan: the top tax avoidance schemes, not to exceed 10, disclosed by whistleblowers during such year

claims.claim: Names the Act the 'IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act.'
claims.sourceSpan:
This Act may be cited as the ``IRS Whistleblower
Program Improvement Act''

claims.claim: Provides that amendments refer to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.
claims.sourceSpan: whenever in this Act an amendment is expressed in terms of an amendment to a section or other provision, the reference shall be considered to be made to a section or other provision of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986

claims.claim: Defines 'Secretary' as the Secretary of the Treasury or delegate.
claims.sourceSpan: the term ``Secretary'' means the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary's delegate

claims.claim: Amends section 7623(b)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to require the Tax Court to review IRS whistleblower award determinations de novo.
claims.sourceSpan: Paragraph (4) of section 7623(b) is amended
claims.note: De novo standard backed by the Section 2 de novo span; removed the pre-reconciliation 'rather than the current abuse of discretion standard' (prior standard not in source).

claims.claim: The amendment requires the Tax Court's review to be de novo, based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination plus any additional newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence.
claims.sourceSpan: shall be de novo and shall be based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination and any additional newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence

claims.claim: It also strikes 'appealed to' and inserts 'reviewed by.'
claims.sourceSpan: by striking ``appealed to'' and inserting ``reviewed by''

claims.claim: It changes the paragraph (4) heading from 'Appeal' to 'Review.'
claims.sourceSpan: The heading of paragraph (4) of section 7623(b) is amended by striking ``Appeal'' and inserting ``Review''

claims.claim: Applies to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) that are pending on or filed after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: apply to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 which are pending on, or filed on or after, the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Adds section 7623(b)(6)(D) allowing a whistleblower to elect to proceed anonymously in all Tax Court proceedings under the whistleblower award section.
claims.sourceSpan: Paragraph (6) of section 7623(b) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph
claims.note: 'may elect ... for all proceedings under this section' backed by the Section 3 election span.

claims.claim: Notwithstanding sections 7458 and 7461, a whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court.
claims.sourceSpan:
Notwithstanding sections 7458 and 7461, a
whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before
the Tax Court for all proceedings under this section
claims.note: Reconciled: removed the pre-reconciliation gloss that sections 7458/7461 make proceedings 'generally public' (characterization of unfetched statutes) and the 'overrides those provisions' framing (Engrossed text is a whistleblower election, not an automatic override).

claims.claim: The election is unavailable if the Tax Court finds that a societal interest in disclosing the whistleblower's identity exceeds the potential harm disclosure could cause to the whistleblower.
claims.sourceSpan:
absent a finding by the Tax Court that a societal
interest exists for disclosing the whistleblower's

could cause to the whistleblower

a societal
interest exists for disclosing the whistleblower's

claims.sourceSpan: apply to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 which are pending on, or filed on or after, the date of the enactment of this Act
claims.note: Sec. 3(b) effective date, reworded in the Engrossed version, matches this prose.

claims.claim: Amends Section 406(c) of division A of the Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006.
claims.sourceSpan:

claims.note: Reconciled: dropped 'annual' qualifier (not stated verbatim); 'during such year' anchors the yearly cadence.

claims.claim: Applies to reports for fiscal years ending after the enactment of this Act.

claims.claim: The bill requires de novo Tax Court review of whistleblower awards but does not set any deadline for the Tax Court to decide a whistleblower petition.
claims.sourceSpan: Any review by the Tax Court under the preceding sentence shall be de novo
claims.note: Gap grounded in Section 2's own subject (standard/scope of review); no Tax Court decision deadline appears in the bill text.

claims.claim: The bill adds interest when the IRS does not provide a preliminary award recommendation notice before the applicable date, but does not set an affirmative deadline by which the IRS must provide that notice.
claims.sourceSpan:

(1) of a preliminary award recommendation before the
applicable date

claims.claim: The bill broadens the attorney's-fee deduction and changes award review to de novo, but does not address how the deduction is treated when a Tax Court review changes the award amount.

claims.claim: Sponsored by Rep. Kelly (R-PA) with 5 cosponsors; de novo review is the provision most likely to draw Treasury/IRS opposition; the five separate changes each add a potential objection point.

resolution: Reconciled the analysis from the superseded Introduced text to the Engrossed (EH, Passed House 2026-04-27) text. Version-driven fix: Section 3 anonymity reflects the Engrossed 'may elect to proceed anonymously' (optional) rather than the Introduced 'shall proceed anonymously' (mandatory), and 'public interest' corrected to the source term 'societal interest'. Source-fidelity fixes on unchanged provisions: removed the unsourced prior-standard 'abuse of discretion'/'unreasonableness' framing on Section 2 (no referencedSource registered); removed 'mandatory'/'discretionary'/'above-the-line' labels on Sections 5-6 that describe subsection contents not stated in the bill text; dropped the 'generally public' gloss on sections 7458/7461; removed editorial framing ('stacked deck','shortchanges','significant') from summary/likelihoodReason; removed the fabricated co-lead 'Thompson D-CA' from likelihoodReason; dropped an unsourced historical-delay clause from gaps. pages recomputed 2 -> 3 (billText 6115 chars).
notes: Audited against data/bill-text/119-HR-7959.txt (Engrossed in House / EH). No referencedSources registered, so all claims are judged against the bill text alone; every statutory characterization of a referenced code section (7623 subsection labels, 7458/7461 effect, prior review standard) was removed rather than sourced from memory. No Congressional Record excerpts in the source file, so featured_quotes/criticisms/comments are out of scope for this bill-text audit. All 49 decomposed claims resolve SUPPORTED against source (0 material, 0 minor, 0 omission).
